lines_of_business: All lines of business unless noted in Program Exceptions
Medicare Advantage: NCD 20.32 TAVR reviewed; no LCD found
criteria_location: Position Statement on pp.2-3 (three paragraphs: native valve, valve-in-valve, cerebral embolic protection) plus a NOTES block immediately after that defines 'severe aortic stenosis' and the FDA risk categories. About 1.5 of 12 pages; the rest is code table, definitions and ~100 references.
procedures_covered: TAVR for native valve aortic stenosis (33361-33369)
Valve-in-valve TAVR for failed surgical bioprosthesis
Cerebral embolic protection during TAVR (33370, investigational)

logic.top_level: pathways (native valve; valve-in-valve) each ALL, plus one NOT (cerebral protection investigational)

k_of_n.quote: severe aortic stenosis is defined by ONE OR MORE of the following criteria

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Native valve: negative leaf 'Member does not have unicuspid or bicuspid aortic valves' inside the ALL list. Cerebral protection: stated investigational.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: None. Valve-in-valve is the only follow-on case (failed bioprosthesis).

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Member is not an operable candidate for open surgery, as documented by at least 2 cardiovascular specialists (including a cardiac surgeon); or member is an operable candidate but is considered at increased surgical risk for open surgery (e.g., repeat sternotomy) due to a history of congenital vascular anomalies and/or has a complex intrathoracic surgical history
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Top-level OR with an inner 'and/or'; the second branch combines 'increased risk' with documentation by two specialists via a trailing clause that may bind to both branches.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: New York Heart Association (NYHA) heart failure Class II,III or IV symptoms
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Equivalent to class >= II; a parser may read 'II,III or IV' as three leaves.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Individuals with Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted operative risk score of less than 3% or 4% are considered at low risk
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: '3% or 4%' leaves a gap between 3% and 4% / 7% and 8%; and none of the risk categories is wired into the native-valve criteria.

definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: For the use of the SAPIEN or CoreValve devices, severe aortic stenosis is defined by ONE OR MORE of the following criteria

definitions_that_change_meaning.term: FDA extreme risk / high risk / intermediate risk
definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) definition of high risk for open surgery: Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted operative risk score of 8% or higher; or Judged by a heart team ... expected mortality risk of 15% or higher
Places patients in one of four categories based on the patient's physical activity limitations

vague_terms.problem: 'See notes' points to the severity thresholds, not to a calcification definition; no imaging method or grading.

vague_terms.quote: increased surgical risk for open surgery (e.g., repeat sternotomy)
For the use of the SAPIEN or CoreValve devices
vague_terms.problem: Severity thresholds are tied to two named devices; other valves (Evolut, Navitor, Portico listed in OTHER) have no stated threshold.
Undefined boundary between low and intermediate risk.

vague_terms.quote: Member does not have unicuspid or bicuspid aortic valves
vague_terms.problem: Negative finding requiring echo/CT; charts often say nothing.

extraction_hazards: Criteria bullets are glyph characters; 'see notes below' separates criteria from definitions
Risk-category definitions in NOTES look like criteria but are not referenced by the position statement
Navigation bar text at top and 'Updates' links
LOINC table adds a code-based documentation rule not found in the prose
Evidence section quotes UpToDate in one long paragraph including phrases like 'not candidates for surgery' that contradict the criteria
interesting_structures: Risk definitions (FDA extreme/high/intermediate/low) are given but the native-valve criteria impose no risk requirement, so low-risk patients appear to qualify
Documentation spelled out as LOINC panel codes with a six-month look-back
Cerebral embolic protection is both a CPT code (33370) and an investigational statement

fit_to_tree.why: Short ALL lists with numeric leaves and one ANY; only the specialist-documentation OR and the orphaned risk definitions need care.
